speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and have an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To help narrow down the cause, can you describe the nature and location of your abdominal pain in more detail? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or heartburn, and have you noticed any skin rashes or itching? Additionally, do you have a family history of cancer or autoimmune disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the fixed, enlarged supraclavicular lymph node and significant weight loss, I need to rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT scan of chest, abdomen, and pelvis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan reveals widespread lymphadenopathy, which strongly suggests a systemic process like lymphoma. I need to confirm the cell type, so REQUEST TEST: Excisional lymph node biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CD20 positivity confirms a B-cell lineage, pointing towards a B-cell lymphoma such as Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. I will now request immunohistochemical stains for BCL2, BCL6, and MUM1 to further subclassify the disease and assess prognosis. REQUEST TEST: Immunohistochemistry panel (BCL2, BCL6, MUM1, Ki-67).

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal immunohistochemical results for BCL2, BCL6, and MUM1 are somewhat atypical for high-grade lymphomas, but the CD20 positivity and clinical picture of widespread adenopathy strongly support a diagnosis of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Given the aggressive symptoms and biopsy findings, I will proceed with the most likely clinical diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
